overview: Free or pedicled fasciocutaneous / musculocutaneous perforator flap from the anterolateral thigh based on perforators of the descending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery (LCFAP-vl nomenclature when the perforator passes through vastus lateralis).
preop: Confirm the recipient defect, recipient vessels and the required pedicle length and skin/fat thickness.
Mark the line from the anterior superior iliac spine to the superolateral border of the patella; the rectus femoris–vastus lateralis septum lies close to this line.
Locate perforators with a handheld Doppler (and CT angiography when available); mark them on the skin. Reported clustering around the midpoint of the line, mostly lower-lateral quadrant (verify).
Look for prior thigh trauma or surgery, and vascular disease or radiation that may affect the pedicle.

steps.title: Position and design the paddle
actions: Supine, thigh slightly internally rotated, hip and knee neutral.
Design the skin paddle with its long axis along the ASIS–patella line, centred on the best Doppler perforator, allowing for the pedicle's route to the recipient site.
structuresAtRisk: Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (subcutaneous, lateral thigh)
pearls: Mark both medial and lateral incision lines and keep the planned paddle width consistent with donor-site closure.

warnings.text: Do not centre the paddle away from the perforator you marked.
warnings.why: A paddle that extends too far beyond the perforator's territory may become ischaemic at the margins.

steps.title: Medial incision and subfascial approach
actions: Incise the medial edge through skin and subcutaneous fat to the fascia lata.
Incise the fascia and dissect in the subfascial plane laterally over rectus femoris toward the rectus femoris–vastus lateralis septum.
Identify the perforators: septocutaneous (in the septum) or musculocutaneous (emerging through vastus lateralis).
structuresAtRisk: Descending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery
pearls: Confirming a suitable perforator through the medial approach before cutting the lateral edge lets you change the plan.

warnings.text: Keep the fascia attached to the flap around the perforator.
warnings.why: The perforator and its small branches travel with the fascia; stripping it can injure them.

steps.title: Select the perforator(s)
actions: Choose the perforator with good caliber and pulsation closest to the paddle centre.
Include a second perforator for a large paddle or when the first is small.
If no usable perforator is found, consider an alternative donor (for example anteromedial thigh) before proceeding.
pearls: Septocutaneous perforators are short to dissect; musculocutaneous ones need an intramuscular dissection.

warnings.text: Do not take a paddle larger than the selected perforator can reliably perfuse.
warnings.why: Distal paddle necrosis follows capturing territory beyond the perforasome without delay.

highlight: descending branch of lateral circumflex femoral artery

steps.title: Intramuscular dissection (musculocutaneous perforator)
actions: Split the vastus lateralis fibres along the perforator's course.
Clip or coagulate muscular side branches with bipolar; keep both venae comitantes with the artery.
Preserve motor nerve branches to vastus lateralis.
pearls: Work from the perforator toward the pedicle, keeping the dissection plane close to the pedicle.

warnings.text: Avoid traction, twisting and monopolar diathermy near the pedicle.
warnings.why: Perforators are thin-walled; traction or heat causes spasm, intimal injury or thrombosis.

warnings.text: Do not divide the motor nerve branches to vastus lateralis.
warnings.why: Loss of function and avoidable donor-site morbidity.

highlight: descending branch of lateral circumflex femoral artery

steps.title: Follow the descending branch proximally
actions: Follow the perforator to the descending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery in the septum between rectus femoris and vastus lateralis.
Divide small branches; dissect proximally for the length required, up to the origin of the lateral circumflex femoral artery if needed.
Free the nerve to vastus lateralis from the pedicle and preserve it.
pearls: Pedicle length and calibre improve toward the LCFA origin; the artery of the descending branch is usually accompanied by two veins.

warnings.text: Check the pedicle for kinks and for any tethering branch before dividing it.
warnings.why: A tethered or kinked pedicle becomes obstructed after inset.

highlight: descending branch of lateral circumflex femoral artery

steps.title: Lateral incision and flap elevation
actions: Incise the lateral edge through the fascia lata.
Elevate the flap in the subfascial plane from lateral to medial toward the perforator, leaving only the pedicle attached.
Thin the flap only away from the perforator, as planned.
pearls: Mark the flap orientation before division so the inset is not reversed.

warnings.text: Do not thin fat directly around the perforator.
warnings.why: Fat lobules near the perforator carry its branches into the subdermal plexus.

steps.title: Perfusion check and pedicle division
actions: Confirm bleeding and colour of the flap edges; use fluorescence angiography if available.
Divide the pedicle only after the recipient site and vessels are ready, to keep ischaemia time short.

warnings.text: Do not clamp or divide the pedicle until the recipient site is ready.
warnings.why: Unnecessary ischaemia time raises the risk of no-reflow.

highlight: descending branch of lateral circumflex femoral artery

steps.title: Close the donor site
actions: Close the fascia lata only if this can be done without tension.
Close the skin primarily if the width allows; otherwise use a split-thickness skin graft over the muscle.
Place a drain and a non-compressive dressing.
pearls: Primary-closure width limit varies; use a reference value flagged 'verify' (about 8–9 cm quoted in the literature).

warnings.why: Tension risks wound breakdown and thigh compartment pressure.

steps.title: Inset and anastomosis
actions: Orient the pedicle without kink or twist; anastomose the artery and both veins when possible.
Inset the flap without tension and place the skin paddle so that it can be monitored.
pearls: Support the pedicle where it crosses mobile tissue.

warnings.text: Never inset with tension or leave the pedicle compressed by a tight tunnel.
warnings.why: External compression of the pedicle is a common cause of venous congestion and flap loss.

perforator.risk: Branches to rectus femoris arise from the descending branch

perforator.relation: Lateral boundary; musculocutaneous perforators pass through it
perforator.risk: Motor nerve injury; bleeding from muscular branches
Denervation of vastus lateralis if divided

perforator.structure: Descending branch of lateral circumflex femoral artery
perforator.relation: The source of the perforators; in the septum
perforator.risk: Injury or traction compromises the flap

perforator.relation: In the subcutaneous plane of the lateral thigh

avoidNecrosis.rule: Use a perforator you have confirmed by Doppler, CT angiography or direct vision
avoidNecrosis.rationale: Reliable flap survival depends on the individual perforator and its connections with neighbouring perforators (Neligan Ch. 23)

avoidNecrosis.rule: Keep the paddle within the perforator's reliable territory
avoidNecrosis.rationale: Survival length depends on dominant vessel caliber, connecting choke vessels and venous return (Neligan Ch. 23)

avoidNecrosis.rule: Keep the perforator and pedicle free of traction, twisting and heat
avoidNecrosis.rationale: Mechanical or thermal injury causes spasm or thrombosis

avoidNecrosis.rule: Preserve both venae comitantes where feasible
avoidNecrosis.rationale: A single vein can fail to drain the flap
A kinked pedicle obstructs inflow or outflow

avoidNecrosis.rule: Avoid pedicle compression by tight closure or tunnel
avoidNecrosis.rationale: Venous congestion is a common cause of flap failure

avoidNecrosis.rule: Monitor colour, capillary refill, temperature, turgor and Doppler signal at intervals set by your unit protocol
avoidNecrosis.rationale: Early detection of a vascular problem allows salvage

avoidNecrosis.rule: Account for smoking, diabetes, vasculopathy and prior radiation
avoidNecrosis.rationale: These factors raise the risk of vascular compromise

monitoring: Handheld Doppler or implantable Doppler per unit protocol
salvage: Return to theatre promptly if congestion or ischaemia is suspected; check the pedicle for kink, compression and hematoma, then revise the anastomosis as needed.

numbers.label: Perforator clustering
numbers.value: midpoint of the ASIS–patella line, mostly lower-lateral quadrant
